To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the orchid R2-R3-MYB transcription factor DwMYB2 is involved in iron uptake and translocation in Arabidopsis, and that the ectopic expressions of DwMYB1 and DwMYB2 affect iron homeostasis of transgenic plants.
the orchid R2-R3-MYB transcription factor DwMYB2 confers Arabidopsis thylakoid iron deficiency response (TIDR) by regulating the expression of iron transporter genes and peptide transporters.

the ectopic over-expression of orchid R-2R-3 MYB gene DwMY B2 in Arabidopisis thaliana conferring the transgenic plants to be more sensitive to iron deficiency, and the iron content in transgenic root is two-fold that in wild-type while the reverse is in shoot.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of iron transport from root-to-shoot and the role of DwMYB transcription factor in this process.
the genetic regulation of plant iron transport and homeostasis.
the genetic regulation of iron homeostasis and allocation in plants, which may provide new insights into the understanding of the mechanism of iron uptake and homeoestasis in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transgenic expression of DwMFB2 in Arabidopsi thaliana conferring hypersensitivity to iron deficient conditions is likely due to the up-regulation of ferric-chelated reductase gene and iron transporter genes and down-regulation of other iron transporter genes.
DwMYB2 regulates iron homeostasis and translocation from root to shoot by modulating the expression of several iron transporter genes and transcription factors.
DwMYB2, a R2R3-type MYB transcription factor, is involved in regulating the whole plant iron homeostasis and the iron transport from root-to-shoot in Arabidopsis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DwMYB2 regulates iron uptake from soil and its translocation from root to shoot by affecting the expression of a set of genes.
DwMYB2 regulates the whole plant iron trafficking by affecting the expression of iron transporters and transcriptional regulators in Arabidopsis.
the ectopic DwMYB2 gene expression in Arabidopsis causes the alteration in iron homeostasis and the expression of genes related to iron transport and peptide transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of iron homeostasis is more complex than what we have thought before.
the expression of DwMyb2 affects the expression of several genes involved in iron homeostasis, which results in the impairment of iron transport from root-to-shoot in Arabidopsis.
the expression of DwMyb2 affects the iron homeostasis and allocation in whole plant.
